propositions.text: The Appellant, a Georgian citizen, appeals the RPD decision denying refugee protection.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX (the Appellant), a citizen of Georgia, appeals a decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) denying his claim for refugee protection.

propositions.text: The Appellant submits new evidence and requests an oral hearing.
propositions.quote: He has submitted new evidence and he has requested an oral hearing.

propositions.text: The Appellant requests the RAD to set aside the RPD decision and find him a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: The Appellant also requests that the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) set aside the determination of the RPD and find that he is a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Appellant, a Georgian citizen, appeals the RPD denial, submits new evidence, requests oral hearing, and asks RAD to set aside RPD decision.

propositions.text: Pursuant to IRPA s.111(1)(a), the RAD confirms the RPD decision that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection and dismisses the appeal.
propositions.quote: Pursuant to section 111(1)(a) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA or the Act), the RAD confirms the decision of the RPD that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection. The appeal is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court confirms the RPD decision denying refugee status and dismisses the appeal under IRPA s.111(1)(a).

propositions.text: The determinative issue in this claim is state protection.
propositions.quote: The panel indicated the determinative issue in this claim is state protection.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the key issue is state protection.

propositions.text: The issue is whether the panel erred in its analysis and decision on state protection availability in Georgia.
propositions.quote: It is clear however from the argument that the issue in this appeal is whether the panel has erred in its analysis and decision regarding the availability of state protection in Georgia.

propositions.text: The Appellant submits an argument regarding the standard of review.
propositions.quote: In addition the Appellant submits an argument regarding the standard of review.

paragraphs.summary: The court identifies the issue as panel error on state protection; the Appellant also argues about the standard of review.

propositions.text: IRPA sets grounds for appeal and remedies but does not specify the RAD's standard of review.
propositions.quote: While the IRPA sets out grounds for appeal as well as possible remedies, it does not specify the standard by which the RAD is to review the decision of the lower tribunal.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes IRPA provides appeal grounds but no standard of review for the RAD.

propositions.text: The RAD now benefits from Federal Court jurisprudence on its role relative to the RPD.
propositions.quote: The RAD now has the benefit of Federal Court jurisprudence which speaks to the appellate tribunal's role in relation to that of the RPD.

paragraphs.summary: The court states Federal Court jurisprudence guides the RAD's role relative to the RPD.

propositions.text: Huruglica established the RAD conducts a hybrid appeal, reviewing all aspects and making an independent assessment, deferring only where RPD has advantage.
propositions.quote: In Huruglica, the Court determined that the RAD is to conduct a "hybrid appeal." It is to review all aspects of the RPD's decision and come to an independent assessment of the Appellant's refugee claim, deferring to the RPD only where the lower tribunal enjoys a particular advantage in reaching a conclusion.

propositions.text: Where RAD's assessment differs from RPD's, RAD must substitute its own determination.
propositions.quote: Where the RAD's assessment departs from that of the RPD, the RAD must substitute its own determination.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains Huruglica requires RAD to conduct a hybrid appeal and substitute its own decision if differing from RPD.

propositions.text: RAD may respect RPD's credibility findings or where RPD has advantage but is not limited to intervening only for palpable and overriding error.
propositions.quote: The RAD is, however, not restricted, as an appellate court is, to intervening on the facts only where there is "palpable and overriding error".

paragraphs.summary: The court states RAD can respect RPD credibility findings but is not limited to intervening only for palpable and overriding error.

propositions.text: RAD will review all RPD evidence and independently assess refugee or protection status.
propositions.quote: The RAD will review all of the evidence in the RPD record and come to its own independent assessment of whether the Appellant is a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court states RAD will independently assess all RPD evidence to decide refugee or protection status.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues for de novo review and no deference to RPD on credibility.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submitted a brief standard of review analysis and argued that the appeal should be considered a de novo review and the RAD should not defer to the RPD even regarding questions of credibility.

propositions.text: The RAD disagrees and notes its view on its role in this appeal.
propositions.quote: The RAD disagrees and notes above its view concerning the RAD's role in considering this appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues for de novo review without deference; the RAD disagrees and states its role.

propositions.text: The RPD panel found the Appellant is not excluded despite Minister's argument on fraudulent travel documents.
propositions.quote: The panel provided a lengthy analysis and found that the Appellant is not excluded from making a claim.

propositions.text: The Minister argued for exclusion based on fraudulent travel documents.
propositions.quote: The Minister intervened in the RPD hearing and argued that the Appellant should be excluded on the basis of his use of fraudulent travel documents.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister argued exclusion for fraud; the RPD panel found the Appellant is not excluded.

propositions.text: The Minister challenges credibility of new evidence but does not request a hearing.
propositions.quote: The Minister makes an argument concerning the credibility of the new evidence provided by the Appellant. The Minister is not requesting a hearing in this regard.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister challenges new evidence credibility but does not seek a hearing.

propositions.text: The Minister submits the Appellant fails to show how new evidence meets s.110(4) requirements or relates to him.
propositions.quote: The Minister submits the Appellant has failed to state how the evidence he seeks to include meets the requirements of section 110(4) of the Act and how it relates to the Appellant.

propositions.text: The Minister submits the Appellant fails to state why RAD should hold a hearing under s.110(6) or if he definitively wants a hearing.
propositions.quote: The Minister further submits the Appellant fails to state why the RAD should hold a hearing under section 110(6) of the Act or if he definitively wants a hearing to be held.

propositions.text: The Minister submits the Appellant's statement about wanting a hearing if RAD does not decide in his favour is insufficient and non-compliant with RAD rules.
propositions.quote: The Minister submits as well that the Appellant's statement that if the RAD does not decide in his favour he wants a hearing, is not sufficient and does not comply with the RAD rules.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister argues the Appellant fails to justify new evidence inclusion or hearing request and does not comply with RAD rules.

propositions.text: The Minister submits the Appellant's case law is missing and errors alleged are not specified.
propositions.quote: The Minister also submits the case law on which the Appellant relies is missing as well as the errors that are the ground for the appeal. The Minister submits it is not sufficient to state the decision contains errors without stating what they are.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister argues the Appellant's case law is missing and errors alleged are unspecified.

propositions.text: The Minister notes the Appellant claims to be unrepresented but submitted English submissions without certified translation.
propositions.quote: The Minister notes that the Appellant claims to be unrepresented, even though he provided submissions in English with no certified translation as evidence that he knows what is being submitted.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister notes the Appellant claims unrepresented but submitted English documents without certified translation.

propositions.text: The Minister argues new evidence should be given no weight and RAD should affirm RPD decision.
propositions.quote: The Minister argues that the documentation submitted as new evidence by the Appellant should be given no weight and the RAD should affirm the original RPD decision.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister argues new evidence lacks weight and RAD should affirm the RPD decision.

propositions.text: The Minister submits RAD is not bound by other RPD decisions and they should be given no weight.
propositions.quote: The Minister notes that the Appellant has provided multiple decisions from other RPD hearings as evidence of no state protection in Georgia. The Minister submits the RAD is not bound by other refugee decisions and these should be given no weight.

propositions.text: The Minister submits evidence regarding state protection in other cases is unknown and claimants' fears differ from the Appellant's.
propositions.quote: The Minister further submits in this regard that the evidence regarding state protection before these panels in these cases is unknown and the subjective fears of various claimants are different from the Appellant's.

propositions.text: The Minister notes the Appellant has not confirmed permission to use or disclose other decisions and failed to keep confidential information confidential.
propositions.quote: The Minister notes that the Appellant has provided no confirmation that he has permission to use and disclose these decisions and he has failed to take steps to keep the confidential information in these decisions as confidential.

propositions.text: The Minister submits other claims have no bearing, are not binding, and do not concern the same profile as the Appellant.
propositions.quote: The Minister submits other claims have no bearing on this one, they are not binding, and they do no concern the same profile as the Appellant.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister argues other RPD decisions are not binding, differ in evidence and claimant profile, and confidentiality is not ensured.

propositions.text: The Minister submits the panel read the NDP evidence and did not cherry pick; it was not required to cite every document.
propositions.quote: The Minister submits that the panel stated it has read the documentary evidence contained in the National Documentation Package (NDP)2 on Georgia and did not "cherry pick" that evidence as alleged. The Minister further submits the panel clearly laid out its reasons and it was not required to refer to every document.

propositions.text: The Minister notes the Appellant asks RAD to reweigh evidence without pointing out actual RPD error.
propositions.quote: The Minister notes the Appellant is asking the RAD to reweigh the evidence without pointing out the actual error committed by the RPD panel.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister submits the panel properly considered NDP evidence and the Appellant fails to identify RPD errors, merely reweighing evidence.

propositions.text: The Minister submits the panel fully assessed the Appellant's personal circumstances and found no forward-looking risk in Georgia.
propositions.quote: The Minister submits that the personal circumstances of the Appellant's case were fully assessed and the panel found no forward-looking risk to the Appellant in Georgia.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister submits the panel fully assessed the Appellant and found no future risk in Georgia.

propositions.text: The Minister submits no analysis shows new evidence relevance or why it was unavailable before RPD decision.
propositions.quote: The Minister submits there is no analysis regarding the proposed new evidence and why it is relevant to this claim and why it was not available prior to the RPD's decision.

propositions.text: The statutory declaration and medical documentation were dated two months before the RPD decision.
propositions.quote: The Minister notes the statutory declaration is dated April 10, 2015,3 almost two months prior to the RPD's decision. The medical documentation is also dated two months before the decision.

propositions.text: The Minister submits the decisions provided by the Appellant are neither probative nor relevant for reasons noted above.
propositions.quote: As well, the decisions provided by the Appellant are neither probative nor relevant to the Appellant for the reasons noted above.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister argues no analysis shows new evidence relevance or unavailability; documents predate RPD decision and are not probative or relevant.

propositions.text: The Appellant seeks to overturn the RPD decision because others from Georgia were recognized as refugees and he was not.
propositions.quote: The Minister submits that the Appellant is seeking to have the decision of the RPD overturned simply because other people from Georgia are being recognized as refugees and he was not.

propositions.text: This reason alone is insufficient for the appeal to succeed.
propositions.quote: The Minister further submits this is not sufficient for the appeal to succeed.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister argues the Appellant wants the RPD decision overturned because others from Georgia were recognized as refugees, but this is insufficient for appeal success.

propositions.text: The appeal should be dismissed for lack of perfection due to deficiencies in the Appellant's record.
propositions.quote: The Minister asks that this appeal be dismissed for lack of perfection as the Appellant's record is deficient

propositions.text: Alternatively, the RPD's decision should be confirmed.
propositions.quote: or alternatively confirm the RPD's decision.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister requests dismissal of the appeal for record deficiencies or alternatively confirmation of the RPD decision.

propositions.text: The Appellant makes no response to the Minister's submissions.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes that the Appellant makes no response to the Minister's submissions.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD notes the Appellant did not respond to the Minister's submissions.

propositions.text: Section 110(4) IRPA limits evidence on appeal to that arising after claim rejection or not reasonably available before.
propositions.quote: Section 110(4) of the IRPA provides that the Appellant may present only evidence that arose after the rejection of his/her claim or that was not reasonably available, or that he/she could not reasonably have been expected in the circumstances to have presented, at the time of the rejection of the claim.

paragraphs.summary: Section 110(4) IRPA restricts appeal evidence to post-rejection or previously unavailable evidence, the court explains.

propositions.text: The Appellant submits three documents as new evidence: an affidavit, a medical document, and five RPD Reasons.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits the following documents as new evidence: (a) An affidavit from XXXX XXXX dated April 10, 2015 (b) Medical document dated April 8, 2015 (c) 5 RPD Reasons

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant submits an affidavit, medical document, and five RPD Reasons as new evidence.

propositions.text: The affidavit dated before the RPD decision is not admitted as it was not shown to be unavailable before and is not sworn.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds this document does not meet the statutory test and is therefore not admitted.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the affidavit inadmissible as it predates the RPD decision, is unsworn, and lacks explanation for unavailability.

propositions.text: The medical document dated before the RPD decision is not admitted as no reason for unavailability is given and it lacks connection to the Appellant.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds this document does not meet the statutory test and is therefore not admitted.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD excludes the medical document as it predates the RPD decision, lacks unavailability argument, and no link to the Appellant.

propositions.text: The RPD Reasons are not binding and not material to this case, so they are not admitted as new evidence.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds this evidence is not material to the case at bar and therefore it is not admitted as new evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD excludes the RPD Reasons as non-binding and immaterial to this case.

propositions.text: The Appellant requests an oral hearing under subsection 110(6) IRPA.
propositions.quote: The Appellant asks that an oral hearing be held pursuant to subsection 110(6) of the IRPA.

propositions.text: Section 110(3) IRPA requires the RAD to proceed without a hearing on the RPD record but allows documentary evidence and submissions.
propositions.quote: Section 110(3) of the IRPA requires that the RAD proceed without a hearing, on the basis of the RPD record, while allowing the RAD to accept documentary evidence and submissions from the Minister and the Appellant.

propositions.text: Subsection 110(6) IRPA allows a hearing if documentary evidence raises a serious credibility issue central to the RPD decision that could justify claim allowance or rejection.
propositions.quote: According to subsection 110(6), the RAD may hold a hearing if in its opinion, there is documentary evidence referred to in subsection 110(3) that raises a serious issue with respect to the credibility of the Appellant, that is central to the RPD's decision, and if accepted, would justify allowing or rejecting the refugee protection claim.

propositions.text: No new evidence was admitted, so the request for an oral hearing is dismissed.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes that no new evidence in support of this claim has been admitted. Therefore the request for an oral hearing is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant requests an oral hearing, but the RAD dismisses it due to no new evidence admitted.

propositions.text: The RPD panel found the Appellant failed to rebut the presumption of state protection after reviewing evidence.
propositions.quote: The panel stated that it had read the documentary evidence in the Board's NDP on Georgia... the Appellant has failed to rebut the presumption of state protection.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD panel found the Appellant failed to rebut the presumption of state protection after reviewing evidence.

propositions.text: The Appellant alleges factual and legal errors in the panel's state protection analysis and accuses it of cherry-picking evidence.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits that the panel's decision contains a number of factual and legal errors, particularly in regard to its state protection analysis and conclusion. The Appellant further submits the panel "cherry picked" from the NDP package the evidence that supports its conclusion and ignored evidence that was contrary to its determination.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant alleges errors and cherry-picking in the panel's state protection analysis.

propositions.text: The panel cited the 2013 U.S. State Department report describing Georgia as a democracy with accountable government and generally law-abiding security forces.
propositions.quote: The panel cited the U.S. State Department 2013 Report on Human Rights in Georgia4 which indicates that Georgia is a democracy. It's government is accountable to parliament and the security force is under the control of civilian authorities. This document further indicates that while there are reports of security forces committing abuses with impunity, it is stated that the security forces are generally considered effective and operate within the confines of the law.

paragraphs.summary: The panel cited the 2013 U.S. report describing Georgia as a democracy with accountable government and generally law-abiding security forces.

propositions.text: The panel cited evidence of enhanced police training including human rights and cooperation with international partners.
propositions.quote: The panel further cited this documentary evidence which indicates there is enhanced police training in the curriculum which includes human rights and the legal basis for the use of force. It is further noted that specialized training on human rights is carried out in cooperation with international partners.5

paragraphs.summary: The panel cited evidence of enhanced police training including human rights and international cooperation.

propositions.text: The panel found police have skills for proper investigations and that the Appellant was offered effective protection despite imperfections.
propositions.quote: The panel found that this documentary evidence establishes that the police are provided with the skills to conduct proper investigations. The panel further found that the Appellant's evidence cited below, as to reports to the police, indicate that although imperfect, the Appellant was offered effective and adequate protection.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found police skilled in investigations and that the Appellant was offered effective protection despite imperfections.

propositions.text: The Appellant alleged he was stabbed by an unknown assailant in 2012 and police investigated after hospital staff called them.
propositions.quote: The Appellant alleged he was stabbed by an unknown assailant on XXXX XXXX XXXX 2012. He was taken to a hospital and medical staff called the police. The police attended the hospital and interviewed the Appellant.

propositions.text: The Appellant told police he was a UNM activist and believed his attacker was from the ruling GD party.
propositions.quote: He told the police he was an activist for the Unit National Movement (UNM) and his unknown assailant was not a local resident as he spoke a different dialect. He also indicated that he believed his attacker was from the Georgian Dream (GD), the current ruling party.

propositions.text: The panel noted no evidence that police stopped trying to find the attacker.
propositions.quote: The panel noted that the Appellant did not provide evidence to suggest the police are not still trying to find his attacker.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant alleged stabbing and police investigation; the panel noted no evidence police stopped searching for the attacker.

propositions.text: The panel found the Appellant was offered adequate protection as police responded promptly after hospital called them.
propositions.quote: The panel found the Appellant was offered adequate and effective protection. The panel noted it was not the Appellant but a doctor who contacted the police and the police immediately responded.

propositions.text: The panel noted little evidence and that the attacker was not local, explaining police failure to find suspects.
propositions.quote: The panel further noted there was very little evidence and given that the Appellant testified that his assailant was not from the local area, it is not surprising that the police failed to find any suspects.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found the Appellant received adequate protection and police promptly responded despite little evidence and a non-local attacker.

propositions.text: The panel rejected the Appellant's claim police would not investigate GD members, noting police initiated a criminal case including allegations against GD.
propositions.quote: The panel noted that the Appellant alleged he told the police the assailant was from GD and suggested the police would not investigate a case involving a GD member. The panel rejected this explanation as the evidence shows the police did initiate a criminal case and did record allegations against the GD.

propositions.text: The panel found the case remains open due to lack of evidence, not police protection of GD members.
propositions.quote: The panel further found that the police would not have done so if they sought to protect members of the GD. The panel found the reason the case has not been closed is lack of evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejected the Appellant's claim police shield GD members, finding the case open due to lack of evidence.

propositions.text: The Appellant alleged kidnapping, torture, and threats in 2012; police investigated after hospital and witness interviews.
propositions.quote: The Appellant alleged he was kidnapped by unknown people and tortured on XXXX XXXX, 2012. He further alleged he was threatened that if he did not stop his political activity he would be killed. He was hospitalized and a doctor called the police. A police letter disclosed by the Appellant indicates they attended the hospital and interviewed the Appellant. They also interviewed the man who found the Appellant in the woods and initiated an investigation which is ongoing.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant alleged kidnapping, torture, and threats; police investigated after hospital and witness interviews.

propositions.text: The panel found police had little evidence and the Appellant received adequate police response despite limited evidence.
propositions.quote: The panel found the police had little evidence to facilitate their investigation and that the Appellant had received a more than adequate and effective police response given the paucity of evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found police had little evidence but gave the Appellant an adequate response despite limited evidence.

propositions.text: The panel was not persuaded police failed to investigate properly as witnesses were interviewed and investigation remains open.
propositions.quote: The panel indicated it was not persuaded that the police were not conducting a proper investigation. The panel noted that the police letter cited above indicates witnesses were interviewed and the investigation remains open.

paragraphs.summary: The panel was not persuaded police failed to investigate properly; witnesses were interviewed and investigation remains open.

propositions.text: The Appellant alleged he was attacked again on XXXX XXXX, 2013, outside the UNM office and hospitalized, with police investigation opened.
propositions.quote: The Appellant alleged he was attacked again on XXXX XXXX, 2013,8 outside the UNM office. He was again hospitalized and the police responded to a call from the hospital and opened an investigation.

propositions.text: Witnesses noted three men from a black Mercedes jeep attacked the Appellant and threatened his family if he did not stop political work.
propositions.quote: they also interviewed witnesses who noted that three men came out of a black Mercedes jeep, attacked the Appellant and threatened trouble for his family if he did not stop his political work.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant alleged a 2013 attack outside the UNM office with hospitalization and police investigation; witnesses described attackers and threats.

propositions.text: The panel found police evidence was vague and could not find police were neglecting their duties given limited evidence.
propositions.quote: The panel found that given the limited evidence it was unable to find that the police were not doing their job in the circumstances.

propositions.text: The Appellant failed to provide police with material evidence.
propositions.quote: The panel noted the Appellant failed to provide the police with material evidence.

propositions.text: The panel asked the Appellant how police would find attackers quickly; he said police have different methods.
propositions.quote: The panel noted the evidence provided to the police was vague and it asked the Appellant how he believes they would find these individuals quickly. The Appellant responded that there are different methods the police can use.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found police evidence vague, Appellant failed to provide material evidence, and police methods were questioned and answered.

propositions.text: The Appellant alleged the Governor of XXXX threatened him with violence after he refused to join GD and did not inform police due to GD connections.
propositions.quote: The Appellant alleged that the Governor of XXXX asked him to join the GD9 and when he refused the Governor threatened him with violence. The Appellant further indicated he did not inform the police of the incident because they are connected to the GD.

propositions.text: There is evidence some UNM members were arrested for political reasons and some police failed to investigate GD attacks on UNM members.
propositions.quote: The panel noted there is evidence that some UNM members have been arrested for politically motivated reasons. It further noted as well two or three incidents mentioned in the documentary evidence when police failed to conduct proper investigations of GD members' attacks on UMN members.

propositions.text: No objective evidence suggests UNM members reporting GD violence are denied protection by police.
propositions.quote: It further noted however it had no objective evidence which suggests UNM members who report violence from GD members are being denied protection.

propositions.text: It is not reasonable that the Appellant would not report the Governor's threat to police.
propositions.quote: The panel found it not reasonable that the Appellant would not report the threat from the Governor of XXXX, a known member of the organization allegedly responsible for all the attacks against him.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant alleged threats from the Governor and police collusion; the panel found no evidence of police denial of protection and found non-reporting unreasonable.

propositions.text: The Appellant alleged another attack in 2013 with hospitalization, police response, questioning, and a police report.
propositions.quote: The Appellant alleged another attack on XXXX XXXX, 2013,10 followed by hospitalization, a police response, questioning of the Appellant and other witnesses, and a police report.

propositions.text: Despite investigations, attacks continued, indicating inadequate protection if police had evidence and failed to act.
propositions.quote: The panel noted that despite criminal investigations, the Appellant continued to be attacked and it therefore could be concluded that the protection offered to the Appellant was inadequate. The panel found however that this would be the case if the police had evidence as to who the attackers were and failed to follow up.

propositions.text: Investigations were opened and ongoing despite paucity of evidence offered to police.
propositions.quote: The panel noted the paucity of evidence offered to the police in regard to all these incidents and further noted investigations were opened and are ongoing.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant alleged another attack with police response; the panel found protection inadequate only if police had evidence and noted ongoing investigations.

propositions.text: The Appellant failed to take concerns to higher authority and did not report Governor's threat to police.
propositions.quote: The panel further noted the Appellant has failed to take his concerns to a higher authority and he failed to take the threat from the Governor of XXXX to the police.

propositions.text: The Appellant alleged receiving threatening calls every two weeks for over a year and initially denied reporting to police, then said he did.
propositions.quote: The panel notes the Appellant alleged that after this threat he received threatening calls every two weeks for over a year. When he was asked if he ever reported this to the police, he initially stated he did not. However subsequently in response to further questioning, he stated he did report to the police.

propositions.text: No police report exists about the calls; Appellant said police pay no attention to UNM members.
propositions.quote: The panel noted there was no police report on this regard and the Appellant explained the police pay no attention to UMN members.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found the Appellant failed to report threats to higher authorities; the Appellant gave contradictory statements about police reporting.

propositions.text: The panel did not find the Appellant credible and drew negative inference from contradictory evidence.
propositions.quote: The panel did not find this evidence credible and drew a negative inference from the contradiction in the Appellant's evidence.

propositions.text: Police provided reports on incidents when Appellant reported being attacked as UNM member by GD members.
propositions.quote: The panel further noted that the police provided reports noted above in regard to the various incidents alleged by the Appellant when the Appellant told them he was a member of UNM and he was attacked by GD members.

propositions.text: The Appellant did not contact police about threatening phone calls.
propositions.quote: The panel found the Appellant did not contact the police in regard to the phone calls.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found the Appellant's evidence not credible, noted police reports on attacks, and that Appellant did not report phone threats.

propositions.text: The Appellant did not contact police when GD members surrounded him, obstructing state protection.
propositions.quote: The panel noted the Appellant indicated in his Basis of Claim (BOC) form that he did not contact the police when GD members surrounded him outside his office. The panel noted this incident followed the four incidents noted above and found it was not reasonable that the Appellant would not call the police when he was face to face with GD members, and his failure to do so obstructed his ability to obtain state protection.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found it unreasonable that the Appellant did not call police when surrounded by GD members, obstructing state protection.

propositions.text: Police provided expected protection in a democratic country; Appellant gave insufficient evidence to suggest otherwise.
propositions.quote: The panel found that given the circumstances, the police provided the Appellant with a level of protection that is to be expected in a democratic country, and the Appellant has not provided sufficient evidence to suggest otherwise.

propositions.text: Appellant had other recourse avenues if dissatisfied with police conduct, including Prosecutor General's Office investigations and appeals.
propositions.quote: The panel further found that if the Appellant were not satisfied with the conduct of the police he had other avenues of recourse. The panel noted that reports of police misconduct are considered by the Prosecutor General's Office and the law requires this office to open an investigation when it receives information about a possible violation. It is further noted that a decision by the Prosecutor's office can be further appealed to a higher level within the office.

propositions.text: Appellant provided no evidence of bringing concerns to Prosecutor General, which was unreasonable.
propositions.quote: The panel noted the Appellant provided no evidence that he brought his concerns to the attention of the Prosecutor General and found this to be unreasonable.

propositions.text: Appellant failed to engage all available recourse avenues before leaving Georgia.
propositions.quote: The panel found that the Appellant failed to engage all of the available avenues of recourse prior to leaving Georgia.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found police protection adequate, Appellant had other recourse avenues but failed to use them before leaving Georgia.

propositions.text: Counsel submitted evidence police failed twice to prevent violence against UNM members, but panel found four police reports outweighed this evidence.
propositions.quote: The panel further noted that counsel in the RPD hearing submitted evidence that on two occasions the police did not intervene to prevent violence against UNM members. The panel found this evidence did not overcome the four police reports which concern their investigations into the Appellant's allegations.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found counsel's evidence of police failure did not outweigh four police investigation reports.

propositions.text: The Appellant failed to rebut the presumption of state protection based on country documents and his evidence.
propositions.quote: The panel found, in the context of country documentary evidence and the Appellant's evidence cited above, that the Appellant has failed to rebut the presumption of state protection.

paragraphs.summary: The panel found the Appellant failed to rebut the presumption of state protection.

propositions.text: The Appellant submits the panel cherry-picked evidence supporting its conclusion and ignored contrary evidence, citing the 2013 U.S. State Department Report.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits that the panel "cherry picked" from the NDP package the evidence that supports its conclusion and ignored evidence that was contrary to its determination. In support of this allegation, the Appellant cites the U.S. State Department 2013 Report on Human Rights Practices in Georgia.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant alleges the panel cherry-picked evidence, citing the 2013 U.S. State Department Report.

propositions.text: The 2013 U.S. State Department Report notes police abuse, poor prison conditions, politically motivated harassment of UNM members, violent protests, and judiciary influence.
propositions.quote: This evidence indicates that among the human rights problems reported in 2013 were police abuse of detainees, poor but improving prison conditions, allegations of politically motivated harassment of UNM members, violent protests at some UNM presidential campaign events and external and internal influence on the judiciary.

paragraphs.summary: The 2013 U.S. State Department Report notes various human rights problems including police abuse and political harassment.

propositions.text: The 2013 Amnesty International Report indicates opposition politicians faced violent attacks, selective prosecution, and police failure to prevent violence.
propositions.quote: The Appellant further cites the Amnesty International Report for 201313 which indicates opposition politicians were subject to violent attacks. This document indicates there are allegations of the selective prosecution and removal from office of figures associated with the UNM. In addition, it was reported that there were a number of violent attacks against opposition party politicians in which the police failed to prevent violence.

paragraphs.summary: The 2013 Amnesty International Report indicates violent attacks on opposition politicians and police failure to prevent violence.

propositions.text: The Amnesty International Report notes reports of torture and ill-treatment of detainees in prison and police custody.
propositions.quote: The document also notes several reports of torture and ill-treatment of detainees in prison and in police custody.

paragraphs.summary: The Amnesty International Report notes reports of torture and ill-treatment of detainees.

propositions.text: The RAD reviewed all evidence on state protection and notes the Appellant provides no specific submissions on police response to incidents.
propositions.quote: The RAD has reviewed all of the evidence in the RPD's record concerning state protection and the actions of the police. The RAD notes the Appellant provides no specific submissions concerning police response to the alleged incidents noted above.

propositions.text: The Appellant alleges factual and legal errors in the panel's decision but fails to specify them.
propositions.quote: The RAD further notes the Appellant submits that the panel's decision, particularly in regard to state protection, contains a number of factual and legal errors, but the Appellant fails to indicate what these errors are.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD reviewed all evidence and notes the Appellant gives no specific submissions on police response or errors in the panel's decision.

propositions.text: The panel acknowledged police abuse evidence and is not required to cite all documentation; no evidence panel ignored evidence.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes, in regard to the Appellant's submission that the panel "cherry-picked" the documentary evidence and failed to note evidence contrary to its findings, that the panel did acknowledge country document evidence concerning police abuse. The RAD further notes that there is no requirement for the panel to cite all the documentation and there is no evidence that the panel did not take all the evidence before it into consideration in rendering its decision.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the panel acknowledged police abuse evidence and did not ignore evidence as alleged.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence is mixed on state protection; police abuse and harassment exist but government took steps to promote accountability after 2012.
propositions.quote: The RAD's extensive review and assessment of the documentary evidence indicates that the evidence is mixed in regard to state protection. The RAD notes there has been police abuse of detainees and politically motivated harassment, but it also notes the government that took office in 2012 has taken steps to promote accountability, in particular in regard to corruption among officials in the former government.

propositions.text: Council of Europe's CPT reported many torture allegations under former government but hardly any after 2012 change of government.
propositions.quote: According to the Council of Europe's Committee for Prevention of Torture (CPT) there were many allegations of torture under the former XXXX government but "hardly any" such allegations following the change of government in 2012.

propositions.text: In September 2012, ombudsman created civil monitoring system for prisons; more disciplinary actions imposed on law enforcement officers.
propositions.quote: This document further indicates that in September 2012, the ombudsman created a system permitting civil monitoring of prisons. It is also reported that more disciplinary actions have been imposed on law enforcement officers than previously.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds mixed evidence on state protection but notes government steps to improve accountability and reduce torture after 2012.

propositions.text: Enhanced human rights training instituted for police; police generally effective despite abuse incidents.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes as well that this document, also cited by the panel,15 indicates that enhanced human rights training has been instituted for the police and that the police are generally effective despite incidents of abuse.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD notes police received enhanced human rights training and are generally effective despite some abuse incidents.

propositions.text: ODIHR March 2014 report indicates Georgian judiciary framework is comprehensive and supports fair trials; all stakeholders welcomed ODIHR engagement.
propositions.quote: The RAD cites also the Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights (ODIHR) March 2014 report on trial monitoring in Georgia.16 This is particularly important as allegations have been made concerning political arrests and prosecutions of officials in the former (UNM) government, and this is pertinent to allegations in the case at bar as well. This report indicates the project is managed from Poland and implemented in Georgia by an international team leader at the invitation of the Georgian Foreign Ministry. The document also indicates that all stakeholders have welcomed ODIHR's engagement. It further indicates that "the legal and institutional framework regulating the Georgian judiciary and criminal justice system in particular is generally comprehensive and provides an increasingly sound basis to conduct trials in accordance with the rule of law principles and international fair trial standards."17

paragraphs.summary: The RAD notes ODIHR report finds Georgian judiciary framework comprehensive and fair, with stakeholder support for ODIHR engagement.

propositions.text: Freedom House report indicates monitored trials of former officials observed due process; some election violations by GD but less than UNM's prior harassment.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes that additional country document evidence from Freedom House18 indicates the trials of former government officials have been monitored by Transparency International. This report indicates that despite allegations by the UNM that the new government is practising selective justice; due process in these arrests appears to have been observed. The report also notes, despite the high level of antagonism between GD and UNM deputies from both parties proved capable of working together on several pieces of legislation in 2012. In regard to the 2013 elections, the Tbilisi-based International Society for Fair Elections and Democracy (ISFED) reported a number of violations by GD members. However, it indicated the number of such cases pales in comparison to the systematic harassment and intimidation of GD supporters by the UNM in the 2012 elections. In regard to trials of UNM former government officials, Transparency International Georgia which monitored these trials reported that both the defence and prosecution had enjoyed equal opportunities to present their cases.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD notes Freedom House report finds due process in trials, some election violations by GD, but less than prior UNM harassment.

propositions.text: 2013 U.S. Department of State Report notes some security force abuses but government took steps for accountability in Georgia.
propositions.quote: The 2013 U.S. Department of State Department Report on Human Rights in Georgia19 cited above by the Appellant, indicates there were some reports that security force members committed abuses with impunity, although the government took steps to foster accountability during the year and the public defender documented cases when use of force by police exceeded permissible limits.

paragraphs.summary: The 2013 U.S. Department of State Report notes some security force abuses but government took steps for accountability in Georgia.

propositions.text: RAD finds it was open to the panel to find state protection in Georgia is adequate and available to the Appellant.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds, on the basis of its review of all of the evidence concerning the Appellant's experience with Georgian police and also the country documentary evidence concerning state protection in Georgia, that although it is not perfect, it was open to the panel to find that the Appellant had failed to rebut the presumption that state protection was and is adequate and available to him.

paragraphs.summary: RAD finds it was open to the panel to find state protection in Georgia is adequate and available to the Appellant.

propositions.text: Appellant alleges he is wanted by police for involvement with XXXX and fears abuse if apprehended and wrongfully convicted.
propositions.quote: The Appellant alleged he is currently wanted by the police for his alleged involvement with the XXXX of XXXX and he fears abuse if he is apprehended and wrongfully convicted solely based on his involvement with the UNM.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant alleges he is wanted by police for involvement with XXXX and fears abuse if apprehended and wrongfully convicted.

propositions.text: Panel cited evidence that former UNM officers are arrested for fraud and corruption charges.
propositions.quote: The panel cited documentary evidence that indicates that former UNM government officers are being arrested on charges of fraud, misappropriation of funds, corruption and other criminal acts associated with their positions of power.

propositions.text: Panel cited evidence that ODIHR monitors trials against former UNM leaders.
propositions.quote: The panel further cites country documentary evidence that indicates the Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights (ODIHR) has been charged with monitoring the trials against former UNM leaders.

paragraphs.summary: Panel cited evidence that former UNM officers face fraud charges and ODIHR monitors their trials.

propositions.text: Panel found police sought evidence on misappropriation and Appellant as close associate called as witness, not persecuted.
propositions.quote: The panel found, in light of the trial monitoring report, it is clear the police were looking for evidence relating to misappropriation of funds and money laundering and therefore it is not unreasonable that the Appellant, who has admitted a close association with the XXXX, would be called in as a witness. The panel found this is not evidence of a persecutory act.

paragraphs.summary: Panel found police sought evidence on misappropriation and Appellant as close associate called as witness, not persecuted.

propositions.text: Panel noted Appellant was slapped by police but this was inappropriate, not persecution or life danger.
propositions.quote: The panel noted the Appellant stated he was slapped by a police officer but found this action, though inappropriate, did not amount to persecution or a danger to his life.

propositions.text: Panel noted Appellant had opportunity to approach Prosecutor General's office but did not.
propositions.quote: The panel further noted the Appellant did have the opportunity to approach the Prosecutor General's office and he did not.

paragraphs.summary: Panel noted Appellant was slapped by police but not persecuted; he had opportunity to approach Prosecutor General but did not.

propositions.text: Appellant agreed to XXXX transaction in 2014; police likely aware and summoned him again.
propositions.quote: The Appellant further stated that in XXXX 2014 he agreed to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. The panel found it was likely that the police were watching the Appellant's movements and were aware that this transaction occurred. Five days later the Appellant was again summoned to the police station and he went into hiding.

propositions.text: Panel found Appellant was evading prosecution as material witness, not persecution.
propositions.quote: The panel found the Appellant was eluding possible prosecution and not persecution as he was a material witness.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant agreed to XXXX transaction; police aware and summoned him; panel found he was evading prosecution, not persecution.

propositions.text: Country evidence shows ODIHR monitoring UNM trials was requested due to political charge reports.
propositions.quote: The panel noted that country documentary evidence indicates that the monitoring of UNM trials by ODIHR was requested by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs after there were reports that charges were politically motivated.

propositions.text: Freedom House reported Transparency International monitored trials and found equal opportunities for defence and prosecution.
propositions.quote: The panel noted that the Freedom House22 has reported that Transparency International (TI) Georgia has "...monitored the ensuing legal proceedings and found that both the defence and prosecution had enjoyed equal opportunities to present their cases."

propositions.text: Monitoring found no significant due process violations or mistreatment in detention.
propositions.quote: The panel further noted the monitoring has not produced any reports of significant violations of due process and there are no reports that those being detained are being mistreated while in detention.

propositions.text: Panel found no indication Appellant would be treated differently if reporting to police for questioning.
propositions.quote: The panel found no indications that the Appellant would be treated any differently should he report to the police station for questioning in relation to the XXXX of XXXX case.

paragraphs.summary: Panel noted ODIHR monitored UNM trials due to political charge reports; monitoring found no due process violations or mistreatment; no risk to Appellant if reporting to police.

propositions.text: Counsel referenced 18 alleged prison ill-treatment cases; only one investigated, no prosecutions.
propositions.quote: The panel noted that counsel in the RPD's hearing referenced 18 cases of alleged ill-treatment in prison documented by the Public Defender. It was alleged that in just one case an investigation was opened and no prosecutions were made.

propositions.text: Panel found allegations unproven and could be unfounded or closed due to lack of credibility.
propositions.quote: The panel noted these are allegations and no reasons were given as to why the 17 cases were dismissed. The panel found it could not assume they were credible as they could well have been unfounded and closed due to lack of credibility.

paragraphs.summary: Panel noted 18 alleged prison ill-treatment cases; only one investigated; found allegations unproven and possibly unfounded.

propositions.text: RAD notes Appellant makes no specific submissions on panel's findings about prison ill-treatment.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes that the Appellant makes no specific submissions regarding the panel's findings concerning this issue.

paragraphs.summary: RAD notes Appellant makes no specific submissions on panel's findings about prison ill-treatment.

propositions.text: Appellant alleges boss asked him to partake in illegal activities; he refused and contacted police.
propositions.quote: The Appellant alleged that he was asked by his boss to partake in illegal activities at work. He further alleged he refused and contacted the police.

propositions.text: Appellant alleges boss threatened him verbally and told him not to go to police; no contact since 2013.
propositions.quote: The Appellant alleged he was verbally threatened by his boss and told not to go to the police but his boss has not contacted him since XXXX 2013.

propositions.text: Panel found no further contact from boss for over a year and no evidence of further interest.
propositions.quote: The panel noted that there has been no further contact for over a year and there is no evidence that the Appellant's boss has any further interest in him.

propositions.text: Panel found Appellant would not be at risk from boss if returned and could report threats to police for protection.
propositions.quote: The panel found that if the Appellant were to return to Georgia he would not be at risk from his boss, and if the boss were to contact him again, he would be able to report the threats to the police and receive the adequate and effective protection he has received in the analysis noted above.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant alleges boss threatened him after illegal activity refusal; panel found no further contact or risk and police protection available.

propositions.text: RAD notes Appellant makes no specific submissions on panel's findings about threats from former employer.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes that the Appellant makes no specific submissions concerning the panel's findings in this regard.

paragraphs.summary: RAD notes Appellant makes no specific submissions on panel's findings about threats from former employer.

propositions.text: Panel found Appellant did not provide clear evidence state cannot protect him from attackers.
propositions.quote: The panel found that the Appellant has not provided clear and convincing evidence that the state is unable to provide him with protection from his attackers.

propositions.text: Panel found Appellant not at risk if he presents to police regarding former XXXX investigation.
propositions.quote: The panel further found that the Appellant would not be at risk should he present himself to the police in relationship to the investigation against the former XXXX of XXXX,

propositions.text: Panel found insufficient evidence Appellant at risk from former employer.
propositions.quote: and that there was insufficient evidence to establish he would be at risk with relation to his former employer.

paragraphs.summary: Panel found Appellant failed to prove state protection unavailable and no risk from police or former employer.

propositions.text: RAD finds it was open to panel to find state protection available and no persecution risk if Appellant returned and participated in investigation.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds, in the context of the analysis above and its review of the evidence, that it was open to the panel to make the findings above concerning the availability of state protection for the Appellant and the lack of risk of persecution if the Appellant returned to Georgia and participated in the investigation concerning the former XXXX of XXXX. The RAD concurs with these findings.

paragraphs.summary: RAD finds it was open to panel to find state protection available and no persecution risk if Appellant returned and participated in investigation.

propositions.text: RAD confirms RPD's decision that Appellant is neither Convention refugee nor person in need of protection; appeal dismissed.
propositions.quote: Pursuant to section 111(1)(a) of the IRPA, the RAD confirms the determination of the RPD that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection. The appeal is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: RAD confirms RPD's decision that Appellant is neither Convention refugee nor person in need of protection; appeal dismissed.
